clue.text: Entrechats at the bar?

parts.note: an entrechat is a ballet leap with the heels beating together, practised at the barre

explanation.surface: A ballet class going through its leaps at the practice rail.
explanation.walkthrough: The ballet picture (heels tapping at the barre) hides the drinker's word for the last drops left in a glass at the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Heeltaps are the small amounts of liquor left undrunk at the bottom of a glass.

clue.text: Jill's greeting to pirate ?

parts.note: Jill of the nursery rhyme would greet her partner Jack with 'hi', and the two words together mean to seize a vehicle

explanation.surface: A girl says hello to a buccaneer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hi, Jack!' is what Jill of 'Jack and Jill' might say; run together it means to seize a plane or ship, as a pirate does.
explanation.definitionFit: To pirate a plane or lorry is to seize it by force, commandeer it.

clue.text: The attempt of James Cook

definitions.meaning: the explorer's ship, sailed to Australia in 1770

explanation.surface: What the explorer Cook tried to do.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means an effort or try, and HMS Endeavour was the ship of Captain James Cook's first voyage.

clue.text: Old English watchman

parts.note: watchman read as a maker of watches, an English clockmaker of the 1600s

explanation.surface: A night guard from Anglo-Saxon times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watchman' looks like a guard, but means a maker of watches: Thomas Tompion, the father of English clockmaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Tompion was a celebrated 17th-century English clock and watch maker.

clue.text: Reward for the honest turner

parts.note: from the idiom about earning money honestly, to 'turn an honest' coin

explanation.surface: Payment owed to a decent woodworker at a lathe.
explanation.walkthrough: A turner is a lathe worker, but the idiom 'turn an honest penny' means earn money honestly.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'to turn an honest penny' makes this coin what the honest earner gets.

clue.text: A chicken from Italy has a team to beat the jumping cow

parts.note: pollo is the Italian word for chicken
a cricket or football side is an eleven

explanation.surface: An Italian chicken dish joined by a sports side, outdoing a leaping cow.
explanation.walkthrough: In the nursery rhyme the cow jumped over the moon; the 1969 mission landed on it, going one better than the cow.
explanation.definitionFit: The spaceflight that put the first men on the lunar surface outdid the rhyme's cow, which only jumped over it.

clue.text: Ancient writer's reed

parts.note: the water plant from which Egyptians made their writing sheets

explanation.surface: The pen of a scribe from long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: A reed pen sounds like the writer's tool, but this reed was the source of the sheets ancient Egyptians wrote on.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nile sedge was pressed into sheets used as writing material in antiquity.

clue.text: Though notedly slow, many take the old ship

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral fifty, a crossword 'many'
the Argo was Jason's ship in Greek legend

explanation.surface: A slow vessel takes on a great many passengers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notedly' means in musical notation: largo is a very slow tempo marking.
explanation.definitionFit: Largo is the musical direction for a very slow, broad tempo.

clue.text: Weekend watchman

parts.note: one who watches, and also the name of a British Sunday newspaper

explanation.surface: A security guard who works Saturdays and Sundays.
explanation.walkthrough: The Observer is a British newspaper published on Sundays.
explanation.definitionFit: A watcher is an onlooker, and the British Sunday paper bears that name too.

clue.text: Eagle's brain

parts.note: Eagle was the 1969 lunar module, whose thinking was done by its onboard guidance machine

explanation.surface: The mind of a bird of prey.
explanation.walkthrough: Eagle was the lunar module of Apollo 11, guided by its onboard machine.
explanation.definitionFit: The lunar module's guidance system was an electronic calculating machine, its 'brain'.

clue.text: Capital decision in the Golden Apple Stakes

definitions.text: Capital decision in the Golden Apple Stakes

parts.words: Capital decision in the Golden Apple Stakes
parts.note: a decision named after a capital city, taken by the Trojan prince who awarded the golden apple to the fairest of three goddesses, as if judging a horse race

explanation.surface: A splendid ruling in a horse race called the Golden Apple Stakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like 'excellent', but it points to Paris, also the name of the prince who awarded the golden apple to Aphrodite in Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the prince Paris chose among Hera, Athena and Aphrodite, giving the golden apple to the last; that verdict is famous.

clue.text: Beginner at home is cautious about it

indicators.note: about means the word for cautious goes round the other piece

parts.note: chary means wary or cautious
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone starting out in a household who is wary of something.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the proverb 'charity begins at home'.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says kindness to others begins at home, so this virtue is the one that starts in the household.

clue.text: Room for tricks and games

parts.note: a sitting room that gives its name to party tricks and party games played in the home

explanation.surface: A space set aside for magic and play.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitting room gives its name to both 'parlour tricks' and 'parlour games', home entertainments.

clue.text: High degree of reporting from 5, 27 on this

definitions.text: High degree of reporting from 5, 27 on this

parts.words: High degree of reporting from 5, 27 on this
parts.note: a launch towards the lunar surface, whose crew reported back from the 1969 mission; 'high' because it went so far up

explanation.surface: A lofty level of news coverage of a famous mission.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1969 mission was a launch to the moon, and its reports came from the highest point any crew had reached.
explanation.definitionFit: A launch aimed at reaching the moon is called by this name, like the Apollo missions.

clue.text: Cutting Grub Street aphorisms ?

definitions.note: an adjective-like hint for the noun: tools used for cutting

parts.note: Grub Street was the London home of hack writers, so it stands for hacks
saws are old sayings or aphorisms

explanation.surface: Barbed sayings from London's hack writers.
explanation.walkthrough: Grub Street, in old London, gave its name to poor jobbing writers; their sayings are hacks' saws.
explanation.definitionFit: These are fine-toothed saws used to cut metal, so they are tools for slicing.

clue.text: A possible cause of impudence

indicators.note: a possible version of the word cause is one rearrangement among many

explanation.surface: Suggesting one reason why someone might be cheeky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A possible' signals a rearrangement of CAUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheek or insolent talk is called this, as in 'none of your lip'.

clue.text: "Dear Child ! If thou appear-.- -by solemn thought " (Wordsworth)

definitions.text: "Dear Child ! If thou appear-.- -by solemn thought " (Wordsworth)

parts.words: "Dear Child ! If thou appear-.- -by solemn thought " (Wordsworth)
parts.note: the missing word from Wordsworth's sonnet 'It is a beauteous evening', meaning not affected

explanation.surface: A line from a Wordsworth sonnet with a gap to fill.
explanation.walkthrough: The sonnet runs 'If thou appear untouched by solemn thought, Thy nature is not therefore less divine'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means unaffected or unmoved, filling Wordsworth's line about the child.

clue.text: A golf-ball on snow is innocently deceptive

definitions.meaning: a pale ball resting on pale ground, how it lies in golf terms
a harmless untruth told kindly, used here as an adjective

explanation.surface: A golf ball lost in snow fools the player harmlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: In golf the 'lie' is where the ball rests; a white ball on snow has a pale lie.
explanation.definitionFit: A golf ball on snow has a pale resting position, and a harmless fib is the same phrase.

clue.text: The eminence in Fenchurch or Ebury Street

indicators.note: in tells us the answer lies inside the run of street names

explanation.surface: A high point found in one of two London streets.
explanation.walkthrough: Fenchurch Street and Ebury Street are in London; the letters run across 'FenchurcH OR EBury'.
explanation.definitionFit: Horeb is the Biblical mountain where Moses received the law, and an eminence is a hill or high ground.

clue.text: Liberal if unconventional type

indicators.note: unconventional means the letters of the word Liberal are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: A political Liberal who is an odd sort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Type' looks like a person, but means a printing system: the raised-dot script for the blind.
explanation.definitionFit: Braille is a system of raised dots read by touch, a form of print for the blind.

clue.text: Blimey, a horse-doctor in the Navy ? So we hear

indicators.note: so we hear means the words are to be heard spoken, not spelt

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation like blimey, and a vet is an animal doctor

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at hearing of a vet serving as a sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cor' is British slang for surprise, like 'blimey'; 'cor, vet' spoken sounds like the small warship.
explanation.definitionFit: A corvette is a small escort warship serving in a navy.

clue.text: In the first place read, next remember, and last this

indicators.note: in says the answer is contained within the words that follow

explanation.surface: An instruction for the order of reading, remembering and finishing.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits across 'nEXT REMEmber'; 'In the first place' and 'last' nod to the two ends, the extremes.
explanation.definitionFit: The utmost or final point is the far end, the outermost.

clue.text: His place of retirement is up on the hill-to avoid the duns ?

indicators.note: on means the reversed piece sits above the next in the column
is up, in a down clue, means the word for a place of retirement reads upwards

parts.note: a bed is where one retires at night
a tor is a rocky hill

explanation.surface: Someone hiding on a hilltop away from creditors.
explanation.walkthrough: Duns are debt collectors; the question mark admits the definition is a description: one who must avoid the duns.
explanation.definitionFit: Duns are people pressing for payment of money owed, and the person who owes it tries to dodge them.

clue.text: That's going round about showing mailed fists

indicators.note: going round means the letters of that's encircle the next piece

parts.note: re is Latin for about, concerning

explanation.surface: A remark about something circulating, which amounts to shows of force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mailed fists' (armoured gauntlets) is an idiom for menaces of force.
explanation.definitionFit: The 'mailed fist' is a figure for intimidation by force, so warnings of harm are that.

clue.text: Early heart transplant ?

indicators.note: transplant means the letters of heart are moved into new places

explanation.surface: An early heart operation.
explanation.walkthrough: Rathe is an old word for early, still met in poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: Rathe is an archaic and poetic adjective meaning coming soon or ahead of time.

clue.text: Jo's sister goes to a French town

parts.note: Jo March's sister in Little Women is Beth
une is French for a

explanation.surface: A girl from Little Women travels to France.
explanation.walkthrough: Béthune is a town in northern France.
explanation.definitionFit: Béthune is a market town in the Pas-de-Calais region of France.

clue.text: Audible disapproval of the demon rum

indicators.note: audible means the word must be heard spoken, not spelt

parts.note: boos are shouts of disapproval

explanation.surface: A temperance crowd jeers at strong drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The demon rum' is a temperance phrase for alcohol in general.
explanation.definitionFit: Temperance campaigners called alcoholic drink in general 'the demon rum'.

clue.text: No elopement by the singer from this her humble home

definitions.text: No elopement by the singer from this her humble home

parts.words: No elopement by the singer from this her humble home
parts.note: an old music-hall song in which the singer refuses to leave her modest home for a suitor, so she won't elope from it

explanation.surface: A singer declines to run away with a lover from her modest dwelling.
explanation.walkthrough: It refers to the Edwardian music-hall song 'I Wouldn't Leave My Little Wooden Hut for You'.
explanation.definitionFit: The song's singer will not leave her modest timber shack for any suitor.

clue.text: See 5
Though withstanding attack he has to yield about the end

indicators.note: about means the word for yield goes round the other piece

parts.note: to defer is to yield or give way
end is a synonym of the end, the finish

explanation.surface: Someone resisting assault yet obliged to give way near the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Though' and 'has to' are link words; the definition is a description of a person, 'he' who withstands attack, as in a sports back or a title holder.
explanation.definitionFit: One who resists an attack, such as a sports back or a soldier holding a position, is this.
